text: If the message were first put through a simple substitution, each letter always becoming the same other letter, and then moved by a route, every copy of a known letter would land on the same carved letter, and different letters on different ones.
Without moving anything, the three Es of the known text sit over three different carved letters. Each route moves them somewhere else; the test asks whether any route lines them up.
23,931 routes: none passes, for a one-for-one substitution or for one with several cipher letters per plain letter. Shuffled coppers pass none either.
